# US-05.4 — Receive usable errors without leaked internals

|                  |                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Epic**         | [EPIC-05 FastAPI Core Service & Agentic Controller](../epics/EPIC-05-api-service.md) |
| **Priority**     | P1                                                                                   |
| **Estimate**     | 2                                                                                    |
| **Status**       | Blocked                                                                              |
| **Owning agent** | `story-builder`                                                                      |
| **Files**        | [backend/main.py](../../../backend/main.py)                                          |
| **Backlog ID**   | STORY-012 (EPIC-005)                                                                 |
| **Requirements** | [FR-17](../../../agile/requirements.md); NFR-5, NFR-7, NFR-13                        |

## User story

**As a** frontend developer,
**I want** predictable safe error responses and correctly configured browser origins,
**so that** my client can handle unavailable services without exposing infrastructure details or opening access to every origin.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Vision failure has a usable status**
Given the analyzer raises `VisionAnalysisError`,
when an analysis request is handled,
then HTTP 502 contains a generic error message with no stack trace, raw SDK payload, project ID or resource path.

**AC2 — Database failure has a usable status**
Given a persistence or history operation raises `DatabaseError`,
when its API request is handled,
then HTTP 503 contains a generic error message and does not claim the report was saved or the collection was merely empty.

**AC3 — Configured origins govern browser access**
Given comma-separated `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`,
when allowed and unlisted browser origins request CORS preflight,
then only listed origins receive permission; if configuration is absent, only `http://localhost:8501` is permitted by default.

**AC4 — Safe diagnostics and credential policy**
Given failures containing sensitive text and any CORS configuration,
when errors are logged and browser responses are produced,
then credentials, image bytes and raw cloud error payloads are absent from logs and responses, and wildcard origins are never paired with credentialed CORS.

## Tasks

- [x] Add CORS middleware to the FastAPI application
- [ ] Load environment configuration and parse `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` with the documented default
- [ ] Map service exceptions through dedicated handlers to generic 502/503 responses
- [ ] Record safe server-side diagnostics rather than raw exception payloads
- [ ] Verify allowed/unlisted preflight behavior and forbid wildcard-plus-credentials policy
- [ ] Add offline error-mapping and leakage tests against both analysis and history

## Current state

There are no service exception handlers. CORS allows every origin and ignores configuration. STORY-012 is blocked on analyzer, database and environment prerequisites.

| Defect                                                                        | Impact                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **BUG-009 — P1, estimate 1:** `allow_origins=["*"]` ignores `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | Browser access cannot be restricted to the configured frontend origins                              |
| No `VisionAnalysisError` to 502 or `DatabaseError` to 503 mapping             | Clients cannot reliably distinguish vision and persistence outages                                  |
| Database currently swallows failures or leaks client-construction errors      | HTTP handlers cannot translate failures consistently until STORY-006 establishes its error boundary |
| No safe diagnostic policy in orchestration                                    | Failure handling has no verified protection against infrastructure leakage                          |

The current middleware does not set `allow_credentials=True`; do not misreport the existing wildcard as a wildcard-plus-credentials violation. The defect is ignoring configured origins. Follow the [FastAPI instructions](../../instructions/fastapi-backend.instructions.md) and [GCP service instructions](../../instructions/gcp-services.instructions.md); raw cloud payloads do not become acceptable merely because they stay server-side. BUG-009 is folded here and its estimate remains separate from the story's 2 points.

## Test cases

| Test                                                                     | Asserts                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_vision_failure_returns_generic_502`                                | Analyzer failure has a safe predictable response                             |
| `test_database_failure_returns_generic_503`                              | Write/read failure cannot masquerade as persistence or empty-history success |
| `test_cors_allows_only_configured_origins_with_local_default`            | Listed origins are permitted and unlisted ones are not                       |
| `test_errors_and_cors_do_not_leak_secrets_or_allow_wildcard_credentials` | Logs/responses are safe and credentialed wildcard origins are forbidden      |

## Definition of done

All four cases pass with mocked services, BUG-009's origin behavior is fixed without changing backlog priority, generic status mapping covers analysis and history, and coverage stays at least 70%. Service errors are translated at their owning boundary before HTTP mapping.
